title: COMPLETENESS-CRITIC supplement — incident-example specificity not covered by genericization-matrix.json
method: Reading-based transversal pass over ng.aiday.policy source documents (.tex), compared against canonical matrix entry ANCHOR-PEER-BREACH-INCIDENTS and a full grep of genericization-matrix.json. Rows below are concrete named incidents / incident scenarios whose suite-specific detail the canonical matrix does NOT already cover.

alreadyCovered: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (Sep 2024)
MOVEit cohort (UCLA, Stanford School of Medicine, Missouri, Rutgers, Georgia, Yeshiva)
Oracle EBS (named as a vector, not as an institution cohort)
2020 European supercomputer attacks / ETH Zurich CSCS
Threat-actor group names FunkSec and RansomHouse (present in matrix JSON)

entries.title: Named ransomware threat-actor groups dating the failure case-set (Cl0p / Interlock)
surfaceForms: ransomware attack claimed by RansomHouse affected central administrative services
The group FunkSec claimed theft of sensitive data and used double extortion
Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (September 2024): Ransomware (Interlock)
The Cl0p group exploited a vulnerability in Progress MOVEit Transfer software
critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Oracle E-Business Suite (CVSS~9.8), used by the Cl0p group for mass data extortion
entries.genericDecision: The case-set names specific threat-actor groups (RansomHouse, FunkSec, Cl0p, Interlock) and a CVSS score (9.8), which timestamp the argument to the 2024-2025 incident wave. Keep the architectural lesson (third-party/supply-chain vulnerability, double extortion, credential compromise) and retain the actor/variant names only as a dated illustrative footnote; the policy claim must not depend on any one group being current. RansomHouse and FunkSec already appear in the matrix JSON, but the group names Cl0p and the variant Interlock, plus the CVSS~9.8 zero-day detail, are not captured anywhere in the canonical matrix.

entries.title: Oracle E-Business Suite 2025 breach cohort with quantified per-institution detail
surfaceForms: Affected institutions included the University of Phoenix (3.5~million records, per its SEC filing), Harvard (1.3~TB exfiltrated), Dartmouth (35\,000+ individuals), University of Pennsylvania, and Baker University, among others
In 2025, a major wave of incidents in higher education was linked to exploitation of critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Oracle E-Business Suite (CVSS~9.8)
Affected institutions included the University of Phoenix (millions of records), Harvard, Dartmouth, University of Pennsylvania, Baker University, and others
entries.genericDecision: The matrix anchor names Oracle EBS only as a vector and never enumerates the 2025 affected-institution cohort. This cohort (Phoenix with 3.5M records / SEC-filing figure, Harvard 1.3 TB exfiltrated, Dartmouth 35,000+ individuals, University of Pennsylvania, Baker University) and the per-institution quantities are concrete, dated case detail. Keep the supply-chain lesson; retain the institution cohort only as an illustrative, sourced list and avoid presenting the quantified records/TB/individual counts as load-bearing (per the no-quantitative-self-reference and anti-vulgarization conventions). The cohort identities are not Luxembourg-bound but are 2025-event-bound.

entries.title: Columbia (2025) phishing / human-factor incident in the root-cause table
surfaceForms: Phishing / human factor (e.g.\ Columbia 2025) & MFA, awareness, and identity governance --- not blanket restriction of academic networks.
entries.genericDecision: The root-cause table cites 'Columbia 2025' as the worked example for the phishing / human-factor cause category. This named incident is not present in the canonical matrix at all (the matrix's incident anchor enumerates Paris-Saclay, Rennes, Sorbonne, Western Sydney, Texas Tech, MOVEit cohort, Howard, Oracle EBS, supercomputer attacks). Keep the cause-category row generic; treat 'Columbia 2025' as a replaceable illustrative exemplar of the phishing/credential-compromise category rather than a fixed anchor.

entries.title: Institution-specific emergency incident-reporting number (9911)
surfaceForms: Mandatory reporting of all incidents/breaches to ISO/CISO; emergency 9911
AI agents recording meetings prohibited; one instance classified as a data breach (DPO + CNPD)
entries.genericDecision: The consolidation note operationalises incident reporting with an institution-specific internal emergency number ('emergency 9911') and a concrete incident scenario where a single AI meeting-recording is escalated to a reportable data breach (DPO + CNPD). The emergency number is a hard-coded local contact that must be parameterized to a generic 'internal emergency / incident-reporting contact' for any non-originating institution; the AI-recording-as-breach scenario is a suite-specific worked incident example that should be retained as an illustration but framed generically (CNPD is the local DPA, already a matrix-covered regulator). Note: the consolidation document is outside the matrix candidate scope (matrix covers only SUITPOLICY/SUITPOLICYSUMMARY/SUITSOLUTION), so neither the number nor the scenario is in the matrix.
